item.title: Krazati (adagrasib) Colorectal Cancer
item.description:
• Summary: Krazati (adagrasib) failed a confirmatory trial in colorectal cancer, jeopardizing its accelerated approval. The KRAS G12C inhibitor did not meet the primary endpoint, casting doubt on its future in this indication.
  • MoAs: Adagrasib: KRAS G12C inhibitor
  • Sources: Endpoints News, Oncology Pipeline

item.title: Pfizer Myeloma and Regeneron Fianlimab
item.description:
• Summary: Pfizer claimed second place in the myeloma order, likely referring to its bispecific antibody Elrexfio (elranatamab). Meanwhile, Regeneron faced another setback with fianlimab, an anti-LAG-3 antibody, adding to ongoing challenges in the immuno-oncology space.
  • MoAs: Elrexfio (elranatamab): BCMA-directed CD3 T-cell engager bispecific antibody. Fianlimab: anti-LAG-3 monoclonal antibody.
  • Sources: Oncology Pipeline, Oncology Pipeline

item.title: Akeso/Summit Ivonescimab Data
item.description:
• Summary: Akeso and Summit Therapeutics announced new clinical data for their investigational bispecific antibody ivonescimab (PD-1/VEGF) at the ASCO meeting. The results demonstrated promising efficacy in non-small cell lung cancer, potentially positioning ivonescimab as a competitive therapy in the immuno-oncology landscape.
  • MoAs: Anti-PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody; inhibits immune checkpoint PD-1 and blocks VEGF-mediated angiogenesis.
  • Sources: STAT News
